{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash -l

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --nodes=1
#   --time=1:00:00
#   -A e3sm
#   -p compute
#   --job-name=cice-qc
#   --output=log-cice-qc.o%j
#   --error=log-cice-qc.e%j

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  --time=1h \
  --queue=compute \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm %j using Flux job id.
exec >"log-cice-qc.o${FLUX_JOB_ID}" 2>"log-cice-qc.e${FLUX_JOB_ID}"

# NOTE: Slurm -A e3sm (account/project) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=cice-qc is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

cd "${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

source /lcrc/soft/climate/e3sm-unified/load_latest_e3sm_unified_chrysalis.sh

export HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE

export BASE=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.column-package.intel/run
export TEST=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.icepack.intel/run

# Slurm used srun; within Flux we run directly in the allocation.
python mpas-seaice.t-test.py "$BASE" "$TEST"
'
"
}
